transcript.text: Hi everyone. Before we can lock the telemetry pipeline policy and proceed to production enablement, I need to follow our go-live checklist. Per the checklist, I need the security owner and the platform finance owner to confirm that our data-handling and operating-cost requirements are met. The current draft policy has 100% sampling, 30-day retention, and raw event payload storage — so I'd like to hear from both of you on whether that's acceptable from your respective perspectives.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a cost issue. While reconciling the platform invoice ten minutes ago, I found that the production payload volume is expected to cost four times the draft estimate. Our approved operating budget supports exactly 25 percent sampling and exactly 14 days of retention, and a cost alert must be enabled. I have not updated the cost worksheet yet, but the current draft policy of 100 percent sampling and 30-day retention would exceed our approved budget significantly.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a data-handling issue. During an unrelated privacy review this morning, I confirmed that the production events contain the fields tax_id and bank_account in three event types. Our approved data-handling rule requires both of those fields to be redacted before storage and requires raw payload storage to be disabled. I have not yet filed this finding in the launch ticket. This means the current draft policy, which enables raw event payload storage at 100% sampling, does not meet our approved data-handling requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

commitments.detail: Update the draft policy to reflect 25% sampling, 14-day retention, redaction of tax_id and bank_account fields, raw payload storage disabled, and cost alert enabled before production enablement.
Ravi to file the data-handling finding (tax_id and bank_account fields in three event types) in the launch ticket.
Clara to update the cost worksheet with the revised production payload volume cost estimate.
